ACID properties (guarantee reliable transactions):
• Atomicity — transaction either fully completes or fully fails. Ex: bank transfer either moves money fully or not at all, never half
• Consistency — data stays valid before/after transaction. Ex: total money in the bank stays the same after a transfer
• Isolation — simultaneous transactions don't interfere. Ex: two people booking the same train seat don't both succeed
• Durability — once committed, data survives even a crash. Ex: a confirmed order isn't lost if the server restarts
• Primary Key — uniquely identifies a row. Ex: Roll Number in a Students table
• Foreign Key — links to another table's primary key. Ex: Student ID in a Marks table pointing back to Students table
Normalization (reduces duplicate data):
• 1NF — every cell holds one single value only (no lists in one cell)
• 2NF — 1NF + no partial dependency on part of a composite key
• 3NF — 2NF + no column depends on another non-key column
